svg.title: CCDASTRO RainCloud device wiring reference
svg.desc: Device photos and labeled connection callouts, with separate noncrossing routes for infrared sensing, rain relay, and isolated 12 volt power monitoring. The Uno is repeated for clarity.
svg.text: Arduino Uno R3 + GY-906 MLX90614 + Hydreon RG-11
Follow the labeled pins. Connection callouts are not physical pin positions; the same Uno is shown twice.
Keep I²C leads short. Verify the module accepts 5 V at VIN.
Same Uno; USB connection to PC / ASCOM
Contacts carry Uno signals only. PWR1/PWR2 use 12 V below.
Dry: NC closed / NO open. Rain: NC open / NO closed.
Uno side · isolated from 12 V return
Confirm package pin numbers from your PC817 datasheet.
Do not connect 12 V return to Uno GND in this isolated design.
D4 LOW = supply present; not full sensor health.
Set RG-11 to Mode 1: “It’s Raining.” Keep its low-power sleep mode off. Verify both relay states on the bench.
Mount the IR sensor with a clear sky view, away from the RG-11 heater; ordinary glass/acrylic cannot cover its aperture.
Bench prototype: cloud estimates require calibration. Relay, wiring and power faults must be tested before unattended use.
Images: Fritzing Uno R3 artwork (CC BY-SA); Hydreon RG-11; ProtoSupplies GY-906 reference module.
Photos identify the devices; follow the terminal markings on your own hardware. The GY-906 photo is a reference unit.
